builtinCredentialProviders.$comment: Credential providers built into Cargo (`BUILT_IN_PROVIDERS`). The `cargo:` prefix is reserved for these; any other `cargo:` name is executed as a program of that literal name. A `[credential-alias]` entry named after one of these is ignored with `credential-alias <name> ... will be ignored because it would shadow a built-in credential-provider`.

credentialProvider.$comment: No restriction on the `cargo:` namespace. An unknown `cargo:` name is not invalid: Cargo falls through to `CredentialProcessCredential::new` and executes a program of that literal name, which resolves wherever `:` is a legal filename character. Rejecting it would catch a typo'd built-in at the cost of rejecting a working configuration, and this schema rejects only what Cargo cannot run. The built-in names are still listed in `builtinCredentialProviders`, which backs the `[credential-alias]` shadowing rule and serves as editor completions.
credentialProvider.title: credential provider
credentialProvider.description:
Credential provider name, command string, or command with arguments: a built-in `cargo:` provider, a `[credential-alias]` name, or the path to a credential provider executable.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/registry-authentication.html)

oneOf.title: provider name or command string
oneOf.description: Provider name, or executable path and arguments split on spaces.

oneOf.title: path and arguments
oneOf.description: Executable path followed by arguments, passed through verbatim. Use this form for a path or argument containing spaces.

prefixItems.$comment: No non-blank requirement: the array form passes element 0 verbatim to the alias lookup, so a `[credential-alias]` entry with an empty or whitespace name is referenced as `credential-provider = [""]` and resolves. The string form is split on spaces and still requires a non-blank value.
